commentary: With market breadth deteriorating to 40 and the deterministic gate registering WEAK, capital preservation takes precedence over aggressive deployment. Stan Weinstein's stage discipline warns that when benchmark indices experience distribution and slip below key moving averages, breakout failure rates multiply across secondary setups. William O'Neil's market direction ('M' in CANSLIM) dictates caution: persistent institutional selling in benchmark heavyweights overrides isolated stock-level setups. While pockets of relative strength persist in Defence and Capital Goods, Jesse Livermore's cardinal rule demands respecting the general tide. In an adverse or unconfirmed tape, strict exposure management, tightening trailing stops, and holding higher cash reserves represent the only prudent risk-first posture until confirmed accumulation reappears.
